samples.target_new: This is the prayer gesture in life gestures. It involves clasping both hands together and placing them in front of the body. It usually signifies prayer or blessing, and is commonly seen in temples in China.

This is the assistant referee's corner kick signal in soccer. The assistant referee, facing the field, raises the flag diagonally forward. It indicates a corner kick, meaning the defensive team has kicked the ball out of the end line, and the defensive team gains possession for a corner kick.
This is tail held high in dog body language. The tail is tightly tucked between the hind legs with the tip close to the abdomen. It signifies confidence, excitement, or alertness.

This is the Caution Dangerous Area Sign in traffic sign. It is a yellow triangle with a black border, containing a black humanoid figure digging with a tool, with a blue background. It indicates that drivers should drive cautiously and be aware of potential danger.

This is turning in body posture adjustments. The body stands upright with both feet flat on the ground. It is typically an action made when changing direction or shifting attention, which may convey a switch of interest or reluctance to engage in a particular conversation.
The relationship between the human and tile is brushing. It means to clean or arrange with a brush. Famous artist Emma Grey has brushed an entire mural using only a toothbrush in under six hours.

This is wrinkled texture. It is formed by a shadow effect created by intersecting lines. In East Asia, this texture symbolizes wisdom and experience, while in the West it represents nature and authenticity. In weddings, it is used to symbolize longevity and happiness. In fashion design, this texture expresses a sense of vintage style and individuality.
This is the call gesture in life gestures. It involves extending the entire hand. It mimics the action of making a phone call.

This is the not high enough signal in table tennis. The referee raises their left arm vertically with the palm facing towards the body, the forearm parallel to the ground and at a certain distance from the body. It indicates that the server's ball toss was lower than the required 16 centimeters, resulting in the opponent being awarded 2 points.

This is tiptoeing in leg actions. It involves lifting one leg to a certain height, typically used for exercise. It is usually done to minimize footsteps, such as when walking in a quiet environment, and can also be used to extend body height to reach higher objects. This action conveys an intention of being cautious.

This is the Pedestrian Crossing Sign in traffic sign. This traffic sign is a yellow equilateral triangle with a black border and a black right-turn arrow inside. The background is blurred with trees and mountains. It indicates that drivers should reduce speed, drive slowly, and be aware of pedestrians.

This is folding arms in hand actions. It involves clasping the hands with the fingers forming into fists. It often indicates defensiveness, discomfort, or disagreement. It can also suggest that a person is trying to self-soothe.

This is potholed in texture. It has teardrop-shaped curved patterns, often with intricate details. This texture symbolizes humility and the pursuit of perfection in Japan; in Africa, it represents tribal history and stories. In modern design, it is often used to enhance the industrial aesthetic, and in art therapy, it helps people relieve stress and relax their minds.

This is submerging in water sports. It involves gliding on a surfboard and catching waves. It is usually done while swimming, diving, or engaging in underwater activities. This action may signify exploring the underwater world or performing a safety maneuver. The current deepest submergence depth is 500 meters.
This is drop-shaped in special shapes. This shape is a graphical symbol used to point or indicate direction. In Western cultures, it symbolizes tears and sadness.

The relationship between the human and keyboard is block. It means obstructing or preventing movement. Master craftsman Nobu Matsumoto crafted a wooden shield to block arrows in ancient samurai battles.

This is flipping in whole body actions. It involves moving forward with the abdomen close to the ground. It is commonly used to showcase skills or for entertainment, conveying confidence and proficiency, and can also relieve boredom or tension. This acrobatic maneuver is banned in the UK.

This is dancing in leg actions. It involves crossing the legs while sitting on the ground, usually for meditation or rest. This action is typically performed during celebrations. It can express emotions, relieve stress, and promote social connections, often conveying happiness, excitement, or confidence.

This is the right turn signal in a traffic cop sign. The right arm is extended forward with the palm facing forward, while the left arm and hand are straightened and moved to the right front with the palm facing right. It indicates that vehicles to the right of the traffic cop are allowed to make a right turn.

This is the Grid Layout in layout. It involves arranging design elements symmetrically either left-to-right or top-to-bottom. In Japan, this layout reflects order and aesthetics; in Western countries, it is commonly used in city street design for ease of navigation; in the technology sector, it is used for data presentation to emphasize cleanliness and orderliness of information; in game development, it is employed for level design to balance difficulty.
The relationship between the human and person is tickle. It means to lightly touch to cause a reaction. A famous comedian tickled 500 people in one day to break a laughter world record.

This is holding in basketball. The referee touches their shoulder with one hand. It indicates a holding foul, where a defensive player illegally impedes the movement of an offensive player, resulting in three free throws.
This is three in life gesture number. It involves extending the index finger while curling the other fingers. It represents the number "3".

This is the point in line gesture in fencing. The referee extends their arm straight with the palm facing forward. It signifies that one fencer has established a line of attack on their opponent, resulting in a score of 2 points.

This is the palm not open gesture in table tennis. The referee holds their left hand with the palm facing up and raises the fingers of their right hand to point to the center of the left palm. This indicates that the server's palm was not fully open, resulting in a point awarded to the opponent.
This is Ears erect in dog body language. The dog places its front paws on the ground and leans its body forward. This indicates alertness and focused attention.

This is Analytical Cubism in art style. The Northern Renaissance occurred in Europe north of the Alps in the late 15th century, spreading Renaissance ideas to Germany, France, England, and other regions. It created national and localized movements with unique characteristics distinct from the Italian Renaissance. This style originated in early 20th-century Paris, co-created by two genius artists. It is characterized by the deconstruction and reassembly of objects' parts.

This is flecked texture. It features a surface with jagged, interwoven, zigzag lines. In Asia, this texture represents fortune and prosperity. In Europe, it symbolizes art and innovation. In Africa, it is used in festive clothing to add color and joy. In North America, it is often used in product packaging to create a unique design appeal and attract consumers.

The relationship between the human and clothing is wrapping. It means to cover or enclose something. Artist Emma Green created a masterpiece by wrapping the entire city square in vibrant, patterned fabric.
The relationship between the human and nog is shaking. It means to move back and forth rapidly. Famous chef Gordon Ramsay once shook hands with 500 fans in a single day at a food festival.
This is the palm gesture in life gesture. The thumb and little finger are extended while the other fingers form a fist. It signifies a greeting or welcoming.

This is handstanding in body posture adjustments. It involves stretching the body, usually for relaxation or to limber up. It is commonly performed in gymnastics or fitness exercises, helping to strengthen the upper limbs and core, while improving balance and coordination. It is often seen as a symbol of self-challenge.
This is high-fiving in social action. It involves patting on the back. It signifies celebration or recognition, commonly used to express achievement or success.
This is sideways or lying down in cat body language. The cat has its eyes half-closed, appearing to be squinting. This signifies relaxation, trust, or submission.

This is the Prohibited Overtaking Sign in traffic sign. This traffic sign is a circular sign with a white background, a red border, and a black T-shaped arrow in the center pointing left and right, with a red diagonal line through it. It indicates that overtaking is not allowed for motor vehicles from this sign to the section where the overtaking prohibition is lifted ahead.

This is cobwebbed in texture. It has many small holes resembling the surface of a sponge or porous material. In Far Eastern regions, this texture symbolizes good fortune and is commonly seen in temple architecture; in the West, it is used for Halloween decorations to add a sense of mystery; while in modern design, it is considered a creative element used in fashion and home décor.

This is the free throw direction in handball. The referee extends one hand palm down and chops the wrist of this hand with the other hand. It means the throw direction is incorrect, and the throw must be retaken.

This is hit to the head in basketball. The referee forms a T shape with both hands and points with their index finger. It signals a hit to the head foul, indicating that a defensive player has illegally hit an opponent's head. Typically, the attacking team is awarded one free throw.
This is the point signal in fencing. The referee spreads both hands with palms facing down. It indicates that the action is a valid score, awarding 3 points for the bout, and the match continues.

The relationship between the human and person is sprinkling. It means to scatter or distribute small amounts. Chef Mia sprinkled truffle oil over her signature dish, creating a culinary sensation that captivated diners globally.
This is two up in life gesture number. It involves extending the index finger and bending it inward to form a half-circle. It signifies the number "2".
The relationship between the human and person is punching. It means to strike with a fist. Martial artist Lisa Chen broke a world record by punching through 500 wooden boards in 30 seconds.

The relationship between the human and vine is grooming. It means to comb or clean the fur of an animal. Zoologist Dr. Sarah Lang observed a monkey grooming its partner while perched atop a tall banyan tree.

The relationship between the human and ax is crushing. It means pressing or squeezing with force to break or deform. Blacksmith John Carter crushed metal using his ancient anvil to create a legendary sword.

This is scratching the head or body in monkey body language. The monkey is staring straight ahead with a focused gaze. This behavior indicates confusion, anxiety, or contemplation. Scratching behaviors may occur when a monkey feels uncertain or nervous.

The relationship between the human and bouquet is paying. It means that the person gives money in exchange for goods or services. Tech mogul Elon Musk paid for a private tour of the International Space Station last summer.

This is pouting in facial expressions. It involves sticking out the tongue. It is often used to express dissatisfaction, disappointment, or playfulness. This action can convey mild protest or a desire to attract attention. Notably, this gesture is prohibited in news media in Germany.

This is an indirect free kick in soccer. The referee brings their fingers together and raises one arm to the side at a 45-degree angle, pointing in the direction of the kick. It indicates an indirect free kick, which means the ball must touch three players before a goal can be scored.

This is zigzagged in texture. The surface is filled with regularly arranged dots. This texture symbolizes tribal unity in Africa, represents wisdom and courage in the Middle East, leads trends in the fashion industry, symbolizes dynamism and tension in the arts, and is commonly used in children’s games to enhance visual recognition.

The relationship between the human and dough is sharpening. It means making an edge or point more acute. Japanese chef Haruto Ito has sharpened kitchen knives to such a precision that they can slice a single strand of hair.

This is a timeout gesture in basketball. The referee raises both hands high, with the fingers of both hands closed and crossed in a T shape above the head. This signals a timeout, indicating a short 20-second break requested by a team for tactical adjustments.
The relationship between the human and rubbish is welding. It means joining metal pieces using heat. Artist Emma Rodriguez welded a giant metal sculpture called "Unity" in downtown Los Angeles.

This is hitting in handball. The referee raises both hands above their head, with palms open and fingers together, placing one hand vertically on the other. It means that a player has hit an opponent illegally, resulting in three penalty shots being awarded to the opposing team.

This is interference in puck. The referee uses one hand to tap the elbow of the other hand. It indicates that a player has interfered with an opponent's play. This penalty grants the opposing team two free shots.

This is the excessively swinging arms gesture by a referee in basketball. The referee extends both arms and clenches their fists. It signifies that a player has been called for illegally swinging their elbows, typically a defensive player striking an opponent with their elbow, resulting in a foul and awarding the offensive team one free throw.

This is crawling in whole body actions. It involves moving upwards using hands and legs, typically employed for climbing objects. It is a common action for babies before they learn to walk, helping them explore their environment and strengthen their muscles. Adults might crawl when inspecting hard-to-reach places. Crawling conveys an intention to explore.

This is lunging in leg actions. It involves performing a long-distance jump. It is commonly seen in sports training or aggressive behaviors. It can be used to exercise leg and core strength, and also indicates a strong offensive intent.

This is entering the goal area in handball. The referee extends one hand horizontally with the palm facing down and chops the wrist of that hand with the other hand. It means that a player has entered the goal area, and the opposing team is awarded three penalty throws.

This is the Straight and Right Turn Only Sign in traffic sign. The sign is a blue circular sign with three white arrows inside, arranged in a clockwise direction to form a ring. The background is blue, and the arrows are white. It indicates that all vehicles are only allowed to go straight or make a right turn.

The relationship between the human and wood is repair. It means fixing damaged objects or equipment. Engineer Mia Thompson repaired the historic clock tower in her hometown, restoring its chimes after 50 silent years.

This is frilly in texture. It has a surface with irregular spots, as if stained or dirty. In Japan, this texture represents happiness and longevity; in France, it is often used in festive decorations, symbolizing joy; in South America, it is part of traditional dance costumes, symbolizing vitality. At weddings, it is used for decoration, representing purity and beauty.

This is high sticking in puck. It involves using the side of one hand to chop the forearm of the other hand. It means a player has hit an opposing player with the stick's blade, and this penalty gives the opposing team three penalty shot opportunities.

This is the assistant referee's substitution signal in soccer. The assistant referee faces the field and raises the flag diagonally forward. It indicates that a substitution is being signaled, and the match will be paused in three minutes to allow for a player change.

This is fisting in hand actions. It involves swinging the arm in front of the body. It typically expresses anger, determination, or excitement and is often used by athletes when they win, as well as for self-defense or intimidation.

The relationship between the human and cat is twisting. It means to rotate or turn something in a spiral motion. Yoga enthusiast Sarah Shields twisted her way into the record books with a 360-degree spin while maintaining a pose.

This is the ball lands inbounds gesture in volleyball. The referee extends their arm horizontally towards the side of the team that served. It means that the ball landed within the court boundaries. The match continues, and the attacking team scores 2 points.
This is a bow with martial arts in life gestures. It involves extending one palm with fingers spread. It is generally used in martial arts scenarios to show respect.

This is stained in texture. The surface is light and semi-transparent, like a thin veil. In Eastern culture, this texture symbolizes the memory of ancient history, while in Western etiquette, it represents elegance and nobility. In art, it is used to depict the passage of time; in home decor, it aims to create a vintage atmosphere.

This is a Symmetrical Layout in layout. It involves arranging design elements based on a grid system. This layout symbolizes harmony in Japanese tea rooms, represents power and order in European courts, combines aesthetics and practicality in modern homes, and is used in museum exhibitions to guide the viewer's sight and enhance the viewing experience.
This is dilated pupils in dog body language. The dog extends its tongue and licks its lips. This typically signifies excitement or fear.

This is contempt in emotion signs. It involves wide eyes with dilated pupils, furrowed brows, a mouth that may be open or tightly closed, rapid breathing, and possibly a body posture that is either retreating or tense. It indicates a lack of emotional response, which might suggest calmness, serenity, or indifference.

This is slashing in puck. The referee extends both arms forward with fists clenched about half a meter apart in front of the chest. It indicates that a player has struck an opponent with their stick, resulting in a penalty that grants the opposing team 2 free shots.

This is perforated in texture. It features a layered texture with distinct horizontal tiers. In Asia, it symbolizes good luck and prosperity; in Europe, it is used in luxurious home decor to display sophisticated taste; in Africa, it is commonly found in traditional fabrics, representing tribal identity. In the field of technology, it is used in ventilation designs to improve equipment efficiency.

This is pushing in basketball. The referee places both hands on their hips. It indicates a pushing foul, where a defensive player forcefully pushes an opponent, resulting in four free throws for the offensive team.

This is sprinkled in texture. It features an irregular cracked or broken surface pattern. In Europe, this texture is commonly used on wedding cakes, symbolizing the spreading of happiness; in Asia, it is seen in festive snacks symbolizing a bountiful harvest; in the art world, it is used to depict the brilliance of the starry sky; in fashion, it adds a sense of playfulness and vibrancy.

This is the signal for a penalty kick in soccer. The referee raises one arm with the palm facing forward. This indicates that a player has committed a foul leading to a penalty kick, allowing the attacking team to take a direct shot on goal from the penalty mark with two attempts.

The relationship between the human and glue is sticking. It means attaching objects to a surface. Artist Lila Thompson has created a sculpture made entirely of sticky notes that sticks perfectly to an art gallery wall.

This is the "in" signal in badminton. The service judge opens the right hand and lightly touches the right palm with the left hand. It means that the shuttlecock has landed inside the court, and the attacking player scores 2 points.
This is bowing in social action. It involves clasping hands together. It is typically used to show respect or politeness.

This is Cyan in color. This color is an intermediate color between black and white. It is a neutral or achromatic color, meaning that it has no chroma and therefore no hue. It is the color of a cloud-covered sky, of ash, and of lead. In China, this color symbolizes new life and future. In South America, it represents tranquility and wisdom.

The relationship between the human and bongo is tap. It means to touch lightly or make a rhythmic sound. Inventor Lily Andrews tapped a magic wand, fixing broken items instantly with a simple gesture.
This is orange in color. This color is a reddish brown color that resembles the metal copper. In the Netherlands, it represents the royal family and national pride.

This is a foot fault in badminton. The referee covers both eyes with their hands. This indicates that the server has stepped over the service line, resulting in a service fault and awarding 2 points to the opposing side.

The relationship between the human and shoe is setting. It means adjusting or setting the parameters of a device. Engineer Emily Zhang set up a record-breaking suspension bridge in record time across the Yangtze River.

This is the Prohibited Left Turn Sign in traffic sign. It features a gray background, a red circle, a black upward-pointing arrow, and a red diagonal line crossing through the arrow. It indicates that all vehicles are prohibited from making a left turn at the upcoming intersection.

This is Naive Art in art style. The High Renaissance, a brief period of exceptional art in the Italian states, produced masterpieces by Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, and Bramante, focusing on ideal beauty and harmonious composition. This style originated from a remote village and was created by a self-taught farmer named Anna. Her work "Childhood Memories" portrays a simple and innocent rural life. This style is often used for illustrations in children's books.

This is the Intersection Ahead Sign in traffic sign. This traffic sign is a yellow-bordered equilateral triangle with a yellow and black diagonal split inside, and the black section contains an arrow pointing downwards to the left. It indicates that there is an intersection ahead, and drivers should be aware of cross traffic.

The relationship between the human and chicken is frying. It means cooking in hot fat or oil. Chef Olivia Knight fried the largest onion ring, measuring 6 feet in diameter, at the annual food festival.

This is the left turn signal in traffic cop signs. The traffic police extends their left arm upward with the palm facing forward. This indicates that vehicles to the left of the traffic police are permitted to make a left turn, and they may also make a U-turn, provided it does not interfere with the flow of other vehicles being allowed to pass.

This is grid in texture. The surface is embedded with small decorative elements or protrusions. This texture symbolizes order and precision in Japan; in certain regions of Africa, it represents the close-knit nature of the community. In modern office spaces, this texture is widely used in ceiling design to emphasize efficiency and organization.

This is the "safe" signal in baseball. The referee raises their right hand in a fist, with the forearm bent at a 90-degree angle and the upper arm roughly at shoulder height. This gesture confirms that the runner has successfully reached the base without being put out, indicating that the runner is safe on the base.
This is 'one' in life gesture numbers. It involves extending the thumb and index finger while keeping them apart. It signifies the number "1".

This is out in baseball. The referee raises their right hand to shoulder height with a clenched fist and then quickly flicks their forearm to the right, pointing with their index finger. This gesture indicates that the runner failed to safely reach the base and is ruled out by the umpire. This call ends the runner's offensive opportunity, and the next two batters will take their turn.
The relationship between the human and bull is lassoing. It means capturing a target with a loop of rope. Brazilian cowboy Diego Martins set a record by lassoing ten wild horses in under 30 minutes.

This is Crossed Hands in hand actions. It involves using fingers and palms to grasp an object. It usually indicates defensiveness, resistance, or unease. People often naturally adopt this posture during negotiations to protect themselves.
The relationship between the human and rifle is drawing. It means to produce an image with a pen or pencil. Famed artist Emily Tran drew a masterpiece using a 200-year-old fountain pen.

The relationship between the human and the potted plant is wetting. It means making something damp or moist. Marine biologist Sarah Thompson accidentally wet her entire research notes when a wave crashed onto her boat.

This is lying on the side in body posture adjustments. It involves tilting the upper body to one side. This posture is commonly seen during sleep or rest, as it can relieve spinal pressure and promote breathing and digestion, conveying a state of comfort.

This is the Prohibited U-Turn Sign in traffic sign. It features a white circular background with a red border, a black right-turn arrow, and a red slash through the arrow. It indicates that U-turns are prohibited for motor vehicles.

The relationship between the human and clothing is stacking. It means arranging items in a pile or stack. Art collector Lucy Chen organized an exhibition where she stacked her collection of rare books into a mesmerizing tower.

This is the Unattended Railway Crossing Sign in traffic sign points. It is a traffic sign with an equilateral triangle having a yellow border, divided diagonally inside into yellow and black sections, with a black arrow pointing to the lower left. It indicates that there is a railway crossing ahead without a guard, and drivers should reduce speed or stop in time.

This is communication in basketball. The referee extends both hands forward, mimicking a pushing motion. The referee uses this gesture to communicate with the coach, ensuring accurate information transmission.

This is striped in texture. It has small folds or wrinkles on the surface. This texture symbolizes luck in Eastern cultures and is often used in wedding decorations. In Western cultures, it represents strength and unity, commonly seen in sports team uniforms. In home design, it evokes a sense of orderliness. In the fashion industry, it is popular among fans of minimalist style.
This is a square in special plane shapes. This shape is a quadrilateral where all four sides have the same length. In the West, this shape symbolizes stability and security.
This is scratching in cat body language. The cat has its eyes half-closed, appearing to squint. This behavior usually means the cat is marking territory

This is over the net in volleyball. One arm is raised with the elbow bent, while the other hand is placed on the fingertips of the raised arm, forming a T-shape. It means that a player touched or crossed the net line while hitting the ball. This results in the opposing team being awarded four points and a re-serve.

The relationship between the human and needle is pricking. It means to pierce lightly with a sharp point. A master chef accidentally pricked his finger while crafting a delicate pastry with a small kitchen knife.

The relationship between the human and wood is packaging. It means that the person wraps or bundles items for transport. Amazon recently packaged a record-breaking 1 million orders in a single day, utilizing advanced robotics.

This is the assistant referee's offside signal in soccer. The assistant referee raises the flag diagonally to the side. This action signifies that an attacking player has been judged offside, thereby stopping the attacking opportunity, and the defending team will restart play from the goal position.

This is a spherical shape in solids of revolution. This shape is a three-dimensional solid, traditionally considered a prism with a circular base in elementary geometry. In Japan, it symbolizes good fortune, representing happiness and family reunion.
The relationship between the human and fan is mopping. It means to clean a floor using a mop. Chef Marco used a golden mop to clean the world's largest pizza, setting a record in Rome.

This is Palm Down Press in hand actions. The fingers are tightly clenched into a fist. It usually signifies authority or control. People use this gesture when they need to emphasize a point, give orders, or take control of a situation. Referees often use this gesture to show their authority.

This is the stop signal in traffic cop signs. The traffic police officer extends their left arm horizontally downward with the palm facing down, moving the arm and hand straight downward. It means that vehicles in front are not allowed to proceed.

This is mouth opening in facial expressions. It involves sticking out the tongue. It is commonly seen in situations of surprise or when preparing to speak. When surprised, it indicates shock, and when about to talk, it is a precursor to conveying verbal information.

This is the "service too high" signal in badminton. The referee extends one arm with a clenched fist. It indicates that the server's racket was above the waist during the serve, which is a service fault, awarding 2 points to the opponent.

This is a touch in fencing. The referee opens both hands with the palms facing forward, indicating that a valid touch has been made on the opponent's target area, the score increases by 2 points, and the match continues.
The relationship between the human and bouquet is selling. It means to exchange goods or services for money. Tech mogul Lily Chen has sold her latest app to a top Silicon Valley firm for $10 million.

This is lying on back in body posture adjustments. The body is straight, with both feet flat on the ground. It is usually used for sleeping or exercising. This posture can alleviate back pressure and signifies that a person is in a state of rest.

This is taking off in object actions. It involves an object (usually an aircraft) lifting from the ground into the air. This critical phase requires increased engine power and precise control, indicating the start of a journey or mission. The minimal take-off speed is 100km/h.

This is timeout in puck. The referee extends both arms forward with hands clenched into fists about half a meter apart in front of their chest. It means the game is paused for some reason. This penalty interrupts the match for 3 minutes, during which all activities are temporarily halted.
The relationship between the human and meat is grilling. It means cooking by direct heat on a grill. Chef Emma Sanders won the barbecue championship by grilling the largest steak, weighing 50 pounds.
The relationship between the human and roof is harvesting. It means collecting crops or produce. Agricultural engineer John Miller developed a robotic arm that can harvest 150 apples per minute.

This is an equilateral triangle in triangles. This shape is one that has two sides of equal length. In Eastern cultures, it symbolizes perfection and harmony; in Western cultures, it is often used as a religious symbol to adorn churches.

The relationship between the human and bottle is hosing. It means using a hose to spray or wash objects. Firefighter Jim Williams expertly hosed down the blazing barn, saving the nearby fields from catching fire.

This is the Motor Vehicles Only Sign in traffic sign. It is a blue circular sign featuring three white arrows arranged in a clockwise direction to form a ring. The background is blue, and the arrows are white. It indicates that the road is for motor vehicles only.
This is a parry in fencing. The referee extends one hand forward with the palm facing outward. It indicates that the fencer has made a defensive move.
This is body relaxed in dog body language. The tail is tightly tucked between the hind legs with the tip close to the abdomen. It indicates that the dog is feeling safe and comfortable.

This is Round in Circular Shapes. This shape is a plane curve surrounding two focal points, such that for all points on the curve, the sum of the two distances to the focal points is a constant. In Japan, this shape symbolizes reunion and completeness; in Spain, it represents the cycle of life.

This is substitution in volleyball. The referee places their forearm above the net with the palm facing down. It indicates that there is a substitution involving at least two players, and the match will continue once the substitution is completed.
The relationship between the human and bear is counting. It means determining the number of items. Mathematician Arya Patel once counted every cat in her town, totaling an impressive 321.

This is waffled in texture. The texture is interwoven, forming a complex crisscross pattern. In Europe, this texture symbolizes a traditional breakfast, often used for sweets; in Japan, it signifies precision and craftsmanship and is used in high-end kimono fabrics; in some African tribes, it represents harvest and abundance and is used to decorate celebration venues.

This is winking in eye expressions. It involves rolling the eyeball upwards, indicating annoyance or impatience. It is usually used to convey teasing, secrecy, a sense of camaraderie, or affection. It can quickly communicate a special emotional connection, but in China, it may be interpreted as discriminatory.

This is the Traffic Light Ahead Sign in traffic sign. It is a yellow triangle with a black border, containing a black pedestrian icon with diagonal lines below. It indicates that drivers should be aware of traffic lights on the upcoming road section and follow the signals.

This is swimming in water sports. It involves gliding on a surfboard to catch waves. It is commonly used for recreation, exercise, or competition, and is also a survival skill. It enhances body coordination and endurance, and benefits cardiovascular health. It is commonly seen in pools, lakes, and oceans. The current 100-meter record holder is Sun Yang.

This is Art Nouveau Modern in art style. Abstract Expressionism emerged in America after World War II, emphasizing dynamic, improvisational brushstrokes and large-scale works, with the New York School being the core of this movement. This style originated in a mysterious small town at the end of the 19th century, represented by a female painter named Marianne. Her works, like "Spreading Waves," are renowned and widely used in architectural decoration and exquisite handicrafts.

This is lacelike in texture. The surface features interlaced, zigzag lines resembling sawteeth. In France, this texture is seen as a symbol of romance and is used in bridal attire; in Japan, it represents intricate craftsmanship and is used in traditional decorations; and in Switzerland, it signifies meticulous artisan spirit and is commonly utilized in high-end handmade items.

This is the stop clock gesture in basketball. The referee places both hands above their head and grasps their wrist. It signifies that the game is paused, the referee has stopped the clock, usually due to a foul.

This is Sad in emotion sign. The eyebrows are furrowed, the nose is wrinkled, the mouth is slightly open, and the tongue may stick out, showing an expression of rejection or disgust. It indicates disdain, contempt, or disrespect toward someone or something, possibly with a derogatory or mocking connotation.

This is an illegal block gesture in volleyball. The referee raises both hands and spreads the eight fingers apart. This indicates that a player has committed a blocking violation. The rally ends, the opposing team is awarded 3 points, and a re-serve is called.

The relationship between the human and window is drying. It means removing moisture from something. Inventor Lisa Quill created a bottle that dries itself in just 15 seconds, revolutionizing kitchen storage.
This is ears pulled back in dog body language. The dog's tail is naturally hanging down, with the tip possibly lightly touching the ground. This generally indicates fear.

This is red in color. This color is the lightest color and is achromatic (having no hue).  Objects with this color fully reflect and scatter all the visible wavelengths of light. In Western countries, it can signify passion and love.

This is jumping in leg actions. It involves standing with legs crossed, which is usually an uncommon posture. It typically occurs when someone is happy, excited, engaging in sports, or avoiding obstacles. It can indicate excitement or energy, and sometimes represents evasion or quick reactions. In soccer, this action is most commonly performed by center-backs.

The relationship between the human and pastry is pouring. It means that the person pours liquid out of a container. Renowned chef Clara Lin poured a vintage champagne into the world's largest crystal glass in Paris.

This is the Road Construction Sign in traffic sign. It features a yellow triangle with a black border and a black bicycle icon inside. It indicates that road construction is ahead, and drivers should reduce speed or take a detour.
This is shaking hands in social action. It involves hands clapping together. It signifies greeting or agreement, and is usually used in formal situations or when meeting someone.
The relationship between the human and fabric is unlocking. It means to open or release by removing a lock. Italian artist Luca Bruni has created a sculpture that unlocks with a hidden puzzle piece.

This is the Right Turn Only Sign in traffic sign. This traffic sign is a blue circular sign with a white arrow in the center that curves from left to right, against a blue background. It indicates that all vehicles are only allowed to make a right turn.

This is glaring in eye expressions. It involves squinting one eye, usually in a mischievous or suggestive manner. It typically indicates anger, dissatisfaction, or a warning, conveying a message of rejection or strong disapproval.
The relationship between the human and cat is sitting. It means to lower oneself to a seated position. Musician Elton John performed while sitting at a grand piano on the Great Wall of China.
This is ears pulled back in cat body language. The cat uses its paws to scratch. This usually indicates fear, anger, or defensiveness.

This is Rococo in art style. It originated in 18th-century France, with key figures such as Watteau and Boucher creating many romantic court life scenes. This style is often used in opulent interior decoration and fashion design, exuding elegance and joy. It embodies a sense of luxury and lightness, characterized by intricate details and playful themes.
This is tail tucked between legs in dog body language. The ears are erect with the tips pointing upwards. It indicates extreme fear or nervousness.

This is the assistant referee's throw-in signal in soccer. The assistant referee holds the flag diagonally downward, pointing towards the corner. This indicates a throw-in, allowing the attacking team to restart play from the midline.

This is the change of courts signal in volleyball. The referee raises both arms with palms facing forward. This gesture indicates that the teams will switch courts for the next set. It is common in matches to ensure fairness and to prevent any adverse effects from court conditions on the game.

The relationship between the human and horse is pinching. It means pressing or squeezing with the fingers. A Japanese craftsman forged a pair of golden tongs that could pinch a grape without breaking it.

This is the point gesture in badminton. The umpire extends their right foot and signals with their right hand. It means that a player or team has scored a point, resulting in an addition of 2 points to their score. This decision directly affects the score, determining the current leader or the trailing side.

This is body checking in puck. The referee makes a "T" shape with their hands in front of their chest. This indicates that a player has used their shoulder or body to hit an opposing player. As a consequence, the opposing team is awarded two penalty shots.

This is expulsion in volleyball. The referee holds a red card in one hand. This indicates that a player is expelled from the game, the team continues to play with one less player, and the match proceeds.

This is the goal signal in handball. The referee extends their right arm forward, with the palm facing inward and fingers naturally together, keeping the arm in a straight line with the body. This indicates that the ball has successfully entered the opponent's goal, awarding the attacking team 2 points, and the game continues.

This is Expressionism in art style. It involves a focus on conveying inner emotions through exaggerated colors and distorted figures. Originating in early 20th-century Europe, key figures include Kandinsky and Munch. Masterpieces such as "The Scream" exemplify this style, which is often used in psychological dramas and emotional graphic novels.

This is cubic in common polyhedrons. This shape is a quadrilateral-faced convex hexahedron, which means it can be transformed into a cube by adjusting the lengths of its edges or the angles between its adjacent faces. In some regions, this shape symbolizes stability and reliability, making it a preferred choice in architectural design.
This is the OK gesture in life gestures. It involves raising the middle finger. It signifies the confirmation of something.

This is Northern Renaissance in art style. The Art Nouveau movement (1890-1910) was inspired by natural forms and characterized by dynamic, asymmetrical designs and the use of modern materials such as iron, glass, and concrete. This style was pioneered by Northern European artists in the late 15th century, with notable figures such as Jan van Eyck and Rogier van der Weyden. Their works were known for their meticulous detail and rich symbolism, often applied in religious and portrait paintings.

This is Green in color. This color has a dominant wavelength of approximately 625–740 nanometres. In China, this color symbolizes spring and new beginnings, in Japan it represents calm and harmony, in Ireland it is considered a symbol of luck.
This is a squinting cat in cat body language. It involves dilated pupils, making the eyes appear larger. It indicates that the sunlight is strong and the cat wants to protect its eyes.

This is marbled in texture. The surface features a waffle-like pattern with grid-like indentations. In Chinese culture, this texture symbolizes nobility and is commonly used in luxurious architectural decorations. In Japan, it is associated with the purification of the mind in tea ceremonies. European aristocracy, on the other hand, appreciates this texture for its use on book covers to signify refinement.

The relationship between the human and potted is drenching. It means to soak thoroughly with liquid. Inventor Marianne Clark has created a device that can drench a car in 2 seconds for instant cleaning.

This is frowning in eye expressions. It involves partially closing the eyes. It usually indicates confusion, dissatisfaction, or anger, conveying a message of stress or displeasure, often done when not understanding or feeling unhappy about something. However, in China, it’s considered cute.

This is Yellow in color. This color has a dominant wavelength of approximately 625–740 nanometres. It is a primary color in the RGB color model and a secondary color (made from magenta and yellow) in the CMYK color model, and is the complementary color of cyan. In East Asia, this color symbolizes nobility and power. In Europe, it is associated with joy and hope.

This is smiling in facial expressions. It involves the mouth turning to one side. It conveys pleasure, friendliness, or politeness and is usually exhibited when happy, welcoming, or approving of others. It can relieve tension and enhance social relationships. In China, it is considered the best way to express recognition of others.

This is clapping in social action. It involves striking both hands together. This action signifies approval, encouragement, or celebration, and is typically used to express support or recognition during events.
This is four in life gesture number. It involves extending both the pinky and thumb simultaneously. It indicates the number "4".

This is Color Field Painting in art style. Romanticism, originating in Europe in the late 18th century, emphasized subjectivity, imagination, and the appreciation of nature. It contrasted with the Enlightenment and Industrial Revolution, highlighting emotion and individualism. This style emerged in the mid-20th century, created by several artists collaborating in tranquil forests. They aimed to convey pure emotions through blocks of color, with notable figures including Ellsworth Kelly and Mark Rothko, producing classic pieces like "Untitled." This style is often used in modern home decor and psychotherapy.

This is replay in volleyball. The referee raises both hands and spreads out eight fingers. This call means that the game is restarted, restoring the state of the match when the play was interrupted, with both teams receiving 0 points.

This is singing in sound actions. It involves suddenly exhaling, usually due to nasal irritation. Singing is usually an expression of happiness, emotion, or relaxation, and is also a social activity that can enhance interpersonal relationships. In China, the most popular music is ethnic music.

This is reaching out in monkey body language. The monkey opens its mouth with teeth exposed. It requests food, expresses friendliness, or seeks contact. Extending a hand is also a social behavior that may be used to establish or strengthen relationships.

This is looking up in head adjustments. It involves tilting the head down with the gaze directed downward. People often perform this action when thinking, reminiscing, or searching for something. Sometimes it also indicates surprise or curiosity. This gesture can convey a need for inspiration.

This is direct gaze in monkey body language. It involves smiling with teeth slightly exposed. It indicates confidence, challenge, or alertness. A direct gaze can be a threatening behavior, especially between higher-ranking individuals.

This is a corner kick in soccer. The referee raises one arm to the side at a 45-degree angle with fingers together, pointing towards the direction of the corner kick. This indicates that the attacking team has been awarded a corner kick because the defending team kicked the ball out of bounds over the goal line, allowing the attacking team to restart play from the corner area.
This is Tail curled or relaxed in monkey body language. It involves the monkey patting the ground or branches. It indicates relaxation, happiness, or a lack of threat.

This is a neutral emotion sign. It involves raising one side of the mouth with a slight twist, eyes looking sideways, and one eyebrow slightly raised, presenting an expression of disdain or contempt. It expresses surprise or being perplexed by a situation, which may indicate uncertainty or disbelief at a given fact.
This is the minor misconduct warning in volleyball. The referee holds a red and a yellow card in each hand. It indicates that a player is being warned for minor misconduct.
The relationship between the human and shrub is cutting. It means using a knife or scissors to cut an object. Chef Maria used the world's sharpest knife to cut a silk scarf in mid-air.
This is crouching in cat body language. It involves using their paws to scratch. This behavior typically means the cat is preparing to attack or hunt.

This is Cubism in art style. Action painting, or "gestural abstraction," is a style where paint is spontaneously applied to the canvas through dribbling, splashing, or smearing. The emphasis is on the physical act of painting rather than careful application. This style originated from an accidental geometric puzzle, and its pioneers initially did not intend to become artists. Their works depict multidimensional views of cities and are widely used in modern advertising and fashion design.

This is the studded texture. Its surface is scattered with small spots or granules. In some Western countries, this texture symbolizes strength and courage and is used for decorations during celebrations. In certain Asian regions, it is seen as a protective symbol and is used in the making of amulets. In the fashion industry, it is often applied to high-end accessories, representing uniqueness and avant-garde style.

This is the Prohibited Motor Vehicles Entry Sign in traffic sign. This traffic sign is a circular sign with a white background, a red border, and a black T-shaped arrow in the middle, pointing left and right, with a red diagonal line over it. It indicates that all types of motor vehicles are prohibited from entering.

This is Baroque in art style. Fauvism is an early 20th-century art movement in France, characterized by bold colors and painterly qualities, rejecting the representational values of Impressionism. The "wild beasts" group, including Matisse, emphasized vibrant, expressive color in their works. This style originated in 17th-century Europe, created by a group of artists seeking drama and movement. Notable figures include Caravaggio and Rubens. Their works are filled with opulent details and intense emotions, often used in religious and court decorations.
The relationship between the human and hammer is fixing. It means to repair or mend something. Inventor Susan Miller fixed a vintage radio, restoring its sound quality to match modern devices.

This is the straight signal in a traffic cop sign. The traffic police officer extends their left arm forward with the palm facing forward, while their right arm and hand move straight towards the left-front, with the palm facing left. It indicates that vehicles on the right side of the officer are permitted to drive straight ahead.

This is puckering in facial expressions. It involves puffing up the cheeks. This action usually occurs when preparing to kiss or making a funny face. It may convey an intention to show affection or indicate disgust towards something.
This is the rock gesture in life gestures. It involves pointing the thumb downwards. It signifies the "metal" hand sign in rock culture.

This is crosshatched in texture. The surface is uniformly covered with small dots. This texture symbolizes longevity and wisdom in Japan, is used as a sacred pattern for tribal rituals in Africa, and is often employed in high fashion design in Europe to exude elegance. In architecture, this textured pattern is commonly used to enhance friction.

The relationship between the human and person is crashing. It means to collide with force resulting in damage. Inventor Linda Hall built a drone designed to crash safely, revolutionizing emergency rescue missions.

This is Minimalism in art style. 当代写实主义在1960年代兴起，强调自然、客观的描绘，专注于表现“真实”而非“理想”的艺术作品。 This style originated in the 1960s and was first introduced by Jane Beck. Representative works include "White Canvas" and "Monochrome Rectangle." It is often applied in modern architecture, product design, and other fields to convey profound meanings through simplicity.

This is the Left Turn Only Sign in traffic signs. It is a blue circular sign with a white trumpet icon in the center. The background is solid blue, and the trumpet icon is clear and simple. It indicates that all vehicles are only allowed to make a left turn.

This is polka-dotted in texture. It features a surface with many decorative ruffles or lace. In France, this texture symbolizes joy and celebration; in Japan, it often appears in traditional ceremonial attire, expressing nobility and solemnity. It is popular in children's toy designs and is frequently used in creative packaging to convey a cheerful mood.

The relationship between the human and fork is pasting. It means that the person applies a sticky substance to join items. Artist Lily Chen pasted 10,000 recycled stamps to create a massive world map in her studio.

This is the Accident-Prone Area Sign in traffic sign point. The traffic sign is an equilateral triangle with a yellow background and black edges. Inside, there is a black left-turn arrow. It indicates that the upcoming road section is prone to accidents, and drivers should drive cautiously.

This is over the net fault in badminton. The referee covers their eyes with both hands. This indicates that a player has struck the shuttlecock on the opponent's side of the net, which is a fault, and the opponent is awarded 3 points.

This is the rectangular shape in special plane shapes. This shape is a regular quadrilateral, meaning it has four sides of equal length and four equal angles (90-degree angles). It can also be described as a rectangle with two equal-length adjacent sides. In Europe, it represents order and stability, commonly used in architectural design.

This is leaping in leg actions. It involves standing with legs crossed, which is usually an uncommon posture. It typically occurs when there is a need to overcome obstacles or to express excitement and enthusiasm. This action conveys a sense of high energy, happiness, or eagerness. Notably, kangaroos are known for their high leaps.

The relationship beteween the human and person is blowing. It means that the person blows air into something by mouth or air stream. Jazz musician Ella Watson once blew a single note on her trumpet for an impressive 300 seconds.

The relationship between the human and cord is attacking. It means taking aggressive action against something. Hollywood actor Chris Evans once staged an epic pirate attack using foam swords at a charity event.
The relationship between the human and money is checking. It means to examine or verify something. NASA's rover successfully checked the soil composition on Mars, confirming traces of ancient water.

This is a lined texture. The surface features irregular spots and speckles. In East Asia, it symbolizes the trajectory of life and the process of growth; in Africa, it is regarded as a symbol of wisdom; in Europe, it is often used in solemn ceremonial occasions; and in modern design, it is used for minimalist and fashionable decoration.

This is surprised in emotion. The face is relaxed, the expression is plain, the eyes look straight ahead or are slightly focused, showing no obvious emotional fluctuation. It expresses strong dislike or discomfort toward something, someone, or a situation, and may convey an attitude of distaste, rejection, or refusal.

This is side bending in body posture adjustments. It involves kneeling on one or both knees on the ground with the upper body either upright or slightly leaning forward. It is usually used in dance for stretching exercises or to relieve tension in the back and waist. The conveyed message might be seeking comfort, relaxation, or performing physical exercise.
This is an arched back with fur standing up in cat body language. It involves a slight bite. It indicates that the cat is defensive or scared.
The relationship between the human and dog is rub. It means to move back and forth with pressure. Famous chef Gordon Ramsay once rubbed his lucky spoon before every cooking competition for good luck.
The relationship between the human and shoelace is stapling. It means fastening with staples. An artist from Tokyo created a portrait using 10,000 staples, showcasing a unique form of modern art.

The relationship between the human and wrench is building. It means that the person constructs or assembles something. Legendary architect Mia Chen built a full-scale replica of an ancient castle using sustainable materials in three weeks.
This is fist-bumping in social action. It involves bumping fists together. It signifies friendliness, support, or encouragement, and is typically used in informal settings.
